value.rationale: The natural integrated cubic Wiener functional is the first nontrivial odd polynomial path moment beyond a linear integral. At a fixed single-site measurement budget, the optimal sign-only and full-value observation times are different, and the theorem determines both uniquely, with exact variance-recovery fractions 21.0708% and 89.2284%. The strict 0.07851-horizon displacement is a substantive sensor-design limit induced by quantization; this exact non-implied benchmark has plausible use in low-information nonlinear stochastic quadrature and polynomial path simulation. It is not a claim that arbitrary binary encoders have the sign optimum, nor a new general SDE convergence theorem.
